mechanism_narrative: A higher current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates restrictive monetary policy, increasing equity discount rates and compressing valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE increases by more than 0.2pp in a month, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for UNRATE change is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust consumer demand, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between RSAFS and HOUST (measured by product of z-scores) is positive, but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained regime (INDPRO < 110.0), industrial output contraction signals reduced production capacity, increasing inflationary pressures and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 110.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor in the regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for housing, supporting economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 40% of periods when HOUST is above its 3-month moving average, or the Rank IC for HOUST is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting Federal Reserve tightening, which compresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 3.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals an overheating labor market, increasing wage pressures and inflation, leading to Federal Reserve tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between PAYEMS and UNRATE (measured by product of z-scores) is positive, but 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle housing boom (HOUST > 1500.0), strong housing demand signals economic overheating, prompting policy tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1500.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for HOUST in the regime is below 0.03.
